lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Riley is waiting for the office shutter to open so they can ask for another house key. Which line of dialogue changes that plan?

FEEDBACK
The shutter line switches the plan from waiting to searching the art room. Alex's news that the shutter is bolted means waiting cannot work, so the next action has to move. A question about the day does not close the office path. After a useful line, you should be able to point to a new action.

WATCH FOR
Polite chat about the day can sound busy and still leave the plan unchanged. Small talk is not wrong in life. In this short scene it uses time without changing what anyone does. A line also fails if it only repeats the want: 'I want to leave' is already known if Alex is stepping toward the gate. Repair the dialogue by naming a fact that shuts one path and forces a different next action.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write two lines about a locked music cupboard where the second line changes the search. The first plan is to wait for the teacher. The second line must make the students look somewhere else. Label the old plan, the line, and the new plan. Do not use the house key or the office shutter. The writing is the evidence. Speaking the lines needs consent and an adult nearby.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

WORKED MODEL

The art room is the only place left from lunch.' New plan: Riley leaves the office and goes to the art-room door. A small-talk version keeps the old plan. Alex: 'Did you have a good day?' Riley: 'It was fine.' They are still waiting. The stronger line does not insult anyone. It removes the office as a choice. Look at each line, sound, movement or role choice that carries the idea.
teaching.rule: Make the arts idea visible: name the element, technique or performance choice you used and say what effect it creates.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

teaching.feedback: The shutter line switches the plan from waiting to searching the art room. Alex's news that the shutter is bolted means waiting cannot work, so the next action has to move. A question about the day does not close the office path. After a useful line, you should be able to point to a new action.
teaching.fix: Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
teaching.guided_attempt: Describe why the warned-against choice weakens the work, then write a stronger choice with a reason.
teaching.misconception: Changing the decoration without changing the artistic idea does not fix the error. Polite chat about the day can sound busy and still leave the plan unchanged. Small talk is not wrong in life. In this short scene it uses time without changing what anyone does. A line also fails if it only repeats the want: 'I want to leave' is already known if Alex is stepping toward the gate. Repair the dialogue by naming a fact that shuts one path and forces a different next action.

teaching.rule: Use an intentionally weak or disrespectful arts choice as a comparison. Name the specific error, then show a clearer or more respectful choice.

teaching.feedback: The new example should use the same arts idea as the model, but with different content or material.
teaching.fix: Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
teaching.guided_attempt: Make or describe one fresh example that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your main choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Dialogue should change the plan, not fill time with small talk. A line earns its place when the next action is different because it was said. Before the useful line, Riley's plan is to wait at the office shutter in case it opens. Alex says, 'The shutter is locked from inside, so waiting will not get us a second key.' That plan change sends Riley to the art room instead. Small talk such as 'How was your day?' can be kind and still leave both people standing at the shutter. You do not need a long speech. One sentence that closes one path and opens another is enough. Write the old plan, the line, and the new plan. The script is the evidence. Speaking it aloud is optional, with consent and an adult nearby. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
